title: Due status vs work order status; Invoice clears a row
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor (view customers; edit customers to raise a work order), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. Open Customers from the top navigation and switch to its "Maintenance reminders" tab. For the location cases use a two-workplace org (on a one-workplace org the location filter is absent).
  3. Rows in due soon / due today / overdue; a not-yet-due row; a row with no work order; a row with a declined work order; a row with a complete-but-not-invoiced work order. Seed by creating work orders from some rows and taking them to those states.
custom_steps:
1. Read the Due status column values, and a not-yet-due row.
  2. Compare the Due status badge with the work order status badge on the same row.
  3. Read the Work Order column for a row with a linked WO, one with none, and one declined.
  4. Read the WO status badge values, including a Complete one.
  5. On a complete-but-not-invoiced row, use Invoice and watch the row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Due status column carries the three badges (due soon, due today, overdue) and is empty for a service not yet due; it is headed "Due status" so it never reads as a work order's status.
  • The Work Order column shows the most recent work order addressing this service as a link with its own status badge; no work order shows a dash; a declined WO stays linked and the row offers Create work order again; a live WO makes it Open work order, a complete one shows Invoice.
  • The WO status badge shows the app's exact status (up to invoicing, including On Hold and Review); a complete-but-not-invoiced row offers Invoice, and the service resets and the row clears only when the invoice exists.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10570 (S13, The worklist); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S13; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S13-R13: “The Due status column carries the asset tab's three badges, due soon, due today and overdue, per S9-R7, and is empty for a service not yet due. It is headed Due status so it never reads as a work order's status”
  • S13-R23: “The two maintenance surfaces carry the same due badges, due soon, due today and overdue, per S9-R7. A work order's status is a different thing and appears only as the badge beside its number”
  • S13-R14: “The row shows the most recent work order on which this service is addressed, whichever path addressed it, as a link with that work order's own status as a badge beside it ... A row with no work order shows a dash. A declined work order stays linked with its badge and the row offers Create work order again. With a live work order linked, Create work order becomes Open work order; a complete one shows Invoice”
  • S13-R25: “The badge beside the work order number shows its status exactly as the app names it, every value up to invoicing, On Hold and Review included. Complete means the work is done and the service has not yet reset; invoicing resets it and the row moves on to its next cycle”
  • S13-R26: “A row whose work order is complete but not invoiced offers Invoice, which opens that work order's invoicing. The service resets only when the invoice exists, so this is the action that clears the row”
